decks.notes: The key concept of this deck is to disrupt the opponent's game plan while ramping up quickly with powerful artifacts like Mishra's Workshop and Moxen. By using cards like Null Rod and Sphere of Resistance to hinder the opponent's ability to cast spells efficiently, the deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with aggressive threats like Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Stonecoil Serpent. With access to cards like Crucible of Worlds and Wasteland, the deck can also control the opponent's mana base and disrupt their strategy even further. Ultimately, the deck aims to quickly establish a dominant board presence and close out the game before the opponent can recover.

The main concept of this deck is to use Underworld Breach in combination with various spells and artifacts to create a powerful combo that can lead to victory. The deck includes cards like Brain Freeze, Manifold Key, and Time Vault to help generate infinite mana or draw through the deck quickly. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion adds an extra layer of consistency to the deck. With powerful cards like Black Lotus, Ancestral Recall, and Force of Will, this deck aims to quickly and efficiently assemble its combo to overwhelm the opponent.

This deck revolves around generating a high amount of mana quickly, using cards like Black Lotus, Moxen, and rituals to power out powerful spells and combo pieces. The goal is to assemble the Storm combo, utilizing cards like Tendrils of Agony and Bolas's Citadel to generate a high storm count and deal lethal damage to the opponent. The deck also includes disruption like Force of Will and Thoughtseize to protect the combo and interact with the opponent's strategy. Overall, the deck aims to win the game through a fast and powerful combo sequence.

This deck focuses on generating a large amount of mana through fast mana artifacts like Mana Vault, Sol Ring, and Moxen, while utilizing card draw spells like Brainstorm and Paradoxical Outcome to draw into combo pieces. The goal is to quickly assemble a powerful board state, using cards like Lórien Revealed and Thundertrap Trainer to disrupt opponents and protect the combo. By efficiently generating mana and drawing cards, the deck aims to win the game through a powerful combo turn or overwhelming opponents with a combination of spells and creatures.

The deck aims to quickly generate a high storm count through various mana acceleration cards and efficient spells like Dark Ritual. It utilizes powerful combo pieces like Tendrils of Agony and Bolas's Citadel to deal massive amounts of damage in a single turn. The deck also includes disruption cards like Thoughtseize and Force of Will to protect the combo and interact with the opponent. With a mix of card draw, tutors, and fast mana, the deck seeks to win the game by assembling its key pieces and executing a lethal storm combo.

The deck focuses on using disruptive spells and creatures to control the game, while also utilizing efficient removal and counterspells to protect its game plan. It aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy, while also generating card advantage through draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time. By utilizing efficient threats like Lavinia and Orcish Bowmasters, along with powerful finishers like Lurrus of the Dream-Den, the deck seeks to outvalue and outlast opponents in a grindy control matchup. With a mix of disruption, card advantage, and powerful threats, Esper Control aims to dominate the late game and secure victory.

The main focus of this deck is to quickly play disruptive permanents such as Thorn of Amethyst, Trinisphere, and Sphere of Resistance to slow down opponents while deploying powerful threats like Lodestone Golem, Golos, Tireless Pilgrim, and Stonecoil Serpent to apply pressure. The deck also utilizes powerful artifacts like Mishra's Workshop, Urza's Saga, and Karn, the Great Creator to generate additional mana and resources. The combination of disruptive elements and efficient threats create a fast-paced aggro strategy that aims to overwhelm opponents before they can establish their own game plan.

This deck focuses on using mana acceleration and artifact synergies to quickly deploy threats and disrupt the opponent's game plan. By combining powerful artifacts like Mana Vault and Moxen with cards like Grim Monolith and Manifold Key, the deck aims to generate fast mana and enable the use of powerful cards like Mystic Forge and Karn, the Great Creator. The inclusion of efficient creatures like Glaring Fleshraker and Patchwork Automaton allows the deck to apply pressure while also disrupting the opponent's resources. Additionally, cards like Sensei's Divining Top and Nettlecyst help with card selection and protection.

The deck focuses on using artifact creatures and artifacts to create a fast and aggressive playstyle, aiming to overwhelm the opponent quickly. It utilizes powerful artifacts such as The One Ring and Nettlecyst to boost the artifact creatures like Grim Monolith and Glaring Fleshraker. The deck also includes cards like Manifold Key and Mystic Forge to generate additional value and card advantage. Overall, the deck aims to establish a strong board presence early on and maintain pressure throughout the game with its artifact synergies.

This Esper Control deck focuses on disruption and removal spells, along with efficient creatures and card advantage. It aims to control the game by countering threats, removing key permanents, and disrupting the opponent's game plan. The deck also includes powerful draw spells and tutors to find key pieces when needed. The deck is designed to be proactive in its control elements while still maintaining card advantage and flexibility to adapt to various situations.

The main focus of this deck is to control the pace of the game using a combination of counter spells, card draw, and disruption tools like Thoughtseize and Sink into Stupor. The deck aims to assemble powerful card combinations such as Tinker into Bolas's Citadel or Time Vault and key cards like Yawgmoth's Will and Necropotence to fuel its game plan. With access to powerful mana acceleration in the form of Moxen and fast mana like Black Lotus, the deck aims to win through powerful combo finishes like Tendrils of Agony or using Karn, the Great Creator to lock out opponents.

The deck focuses on quickly milling and sacrificing cards from the library, using cards like Balustrade Spy and Undercity Informer to set up the win condition with Thassa's Oracle or Fell the Profane. It aims to combo off without relying on lands, utilizing fast mana sources like Chrome Mox and the Moxen to cast spells quickly and disrupt opponents with Force of Will and Pact of Negation. The deck is built around a powerful deterministic combo that can win the game in a single turn, leading to a swift victory in Vintage 1 vs 1 matchups.

The main concept of this Esper Control deck is to use powerful spells such as Ancestral Recall, Time Walk, and Force of Will to control the game and disrupt opponent's strategies. The deck also includes efficient removal in the form of Swords to Plowshares and Lavinia, Azorius Renegade to handle threats. The inclusion of cards like Nihil Spellbomb and Psychic Frog allows for graveyard hate and card advantage, while mana denial with cards like Strip Mine and Wasteland helps gain tempo. Overall, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while building up its own resources for a win.

This Dimir Control deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan by utilizing countermagic, removal spells, and resource denial tactics. By combining powerful spells like Force of Will and Fatal Push with disruptive cards like Null Rod and Strip Mine, the deck aims to control the tempo of the game and outvalue the opponent. Lurrus of the Dream-Den also provides additional value by allowing the player to recast key cards from the graveyard. Overall, this deck seeks to establish a dominant board presence while limiting the opponent's options through disruption and control elements.

The deck focuses on using cards like Stinkweed Imp, Golgari Thug, and Bazaar of Baghdad to enable the Dredge mechanic, filling the graveyard with cards like Narcomoeba and Prized Amalgam. Through a combination of self-mill and graveyard recursion effects, the deck aims to quickly fill the board with creatures like Ichorid and Hollow One, while also disrupting opponents with cards like Force of Will and Grief. The end goal is to overwhelm the opponent with a powerful board state and close out the game with cards like Creeping Chill and Silversmote Ghoul.

This Esper Control deck focuses on efficient removal, card advantage, and disruption to control the game and outvalue the opponent. It utilizes powerful cards such as Ancestral Recall, Time Walk, and Dig Through Time for card advantage and extra turns, while also packing Force of Will and Force of Negation for interaction. Additionally, the deck includes disruptive elements like Null Rod and Wasteland to disrupt the opponent's game plan. The deck aims to control the board and outgrind the opponent with its versatile card selection and powerful spells.
